name: Social login (OAuth and OpenID Connect)
needs: let users log in with GitHub or Apple
Google login made a second account for an existing user
summary: Users sign in with an account they already have. Your app sends them to the provider, gets back a code, and swaps it on the server for tokens that say who they are. Use a library for this, keep the requested permissions small, and only link to an existing account when the provider says the email is verified.
need_when: You want sign-up with no password and less friction.
Your users are businesses that expect Google or Microsoft sign-in.
skip_when: Your users don't have, or don't want to use, those accounts. Offer email sign-in too.

ways.title: An auth library in your framework
ways.how: django-allauth, Auth.js or Better Auth. They handle the code flow, state, PKCE and account linking.
ways.tradeoff: Your data stays in your database. You still register an app with each provider and set exact redirect URLs.

ways.title: A hosted auth service
ways.how: Clerk, Auth0, Supabase Auth or Firebase Auth add many providers from a dashboard.
ways.tradeoff: Fastest. Your user list lives with them and pricing grows with users.

ways.title: A self-hosted identity provider
ways.how: Keycloak, Authentik or Zitadel run on your server and speak OpenID Connect to your apps.
ways.tradeoff: Good when several apps share one login. Heavy to run for a single app.

prompt:
Add [Google] sign-in using [library].

Requirements:
- Use the authorization code flow with PKCE and a state parameter. No implicit flow.
- Ask only for openid, email and profile. Ask for other permissions later, when a feature needs them.
- Register exact redirect URIs for each environment. No wildcards.
- If the email matches an existing account, link them only when the provider marks the email as verified. Otherwise refuse and explain.
- Keep the provider's client secret in an environment variable.
- Show a friendly error page when the user cancels or the provider fails, and log the provider's error code.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. A new Google user who signs in twice still has one account.
2. An existing email user who signs in with Google (verified email) lands in their existing account, not a new one.
3. A callback with a wrong or missing state value is rejected.
4. The consent screen asks only for basic profile and email.
5. Canceling on the provider's screen shows our error page, not a stack trace.
acceptance_checks: A new Google user who signs in twice still has one account.
An existing email user who signs in with Google (verified email) lands in their existing account, not a new one.
A callback with a wrong or missing state value is rejected.
The consent screen asks only for basic profile and email.
Canceling on the provider's screen shows our error page, not a stack trace.
if_you_skip_it: Duplicate accounts, account takeover through an unverified email, or a consent screen asking for far more than you need.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal uses django-allauth with Google as the only social provider. PKCE is on, sign-in asks only for profile and email, and calendar access is requested separately inside the app. The Google prompt is set to select_account so the wrong browser account isn't reused. A verified Google email can sign in to an existing account with the same email.
